fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. John says they “…sang a new song before the throne…” and the sound he hears is like many waters, thunder and harpists strumming their harps. No one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth. I'd pay good money for a front row seat.

I can see why you'd think that, since John says the sound is like the loud rumbling of thunder. But the text doesn't call it a song of mourning. John says it's a new song, sung before the throne, the four living creatures and the elders.
Yes, baker. John says of the 144,000, “They follow the Lamb wherever He goes.” Wherever He goes is the verse's own wording.
You got it, baker. The second angel says, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great…” He says the word fallen twice.
Not quite, friend. The angel announces, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great…” Rising again isn't part of what he says.

That's right, baker. The third angel warns that anyone who worships the beast and its image and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand “…will drink the wine of God’s anger…” This is a heavy warning, so let's take it seriously and move on carefully.

That one sounds familiar, baker, but it's not in this verse. The voice from heaven tells John to write, “Blessed are the dead…” and the verse goes on to say those who die in the Lord from this moment on. Staying awake isn't in that line.
That's a fair guess, friend, but the Spirit's word is rest. The line says, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.” Return isn't the word the Spirit uses.
That's a good one to remember, but it's not in this verse. John says the One on the cloud has a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand. A rod of iron isn't mentioned in this verse.
That's it, baker. The angel cries out, “…the time has come to harvest, for the crop of the earth is ripe.” Ripe is the reason he gives.

The seventh seal is opened earlier in the book (Revelation 8:1), baker, but it's not the reason here. The angel says, “…the time has come to harvest, for the crop of the earth is ripe.” That's the reason he gives.
Yes, baker. The text says, “…the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested.” The angel's call and the swing go together. Verse 16 says it plainly.
Close, friend, but this one is true. John says, “So the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested.” He swings it over the earth, just like the card says.

Wheat and barns feel like they belong in a harvest, friend. But the angel from the altar tells the other angel to gather clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth. Wheat and barns aren't mentioned in this verse.

Sheaves would fit another harvest scene, baker. Here, though, the angel says to gather the clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe. Sheaves aren't mentioned in these words.

The altar does show up in this scene, friend, since the angel with authority over the fire came from it. But the grapes go somewhere else. The angel threw them into the great winepress of God's wrath.
